summary: A 1937 steel Aermotor tower on the Targhee National Forest that saw heavy use in the 1988 Yellowstone fires and is now on standby, listed on the NHLR.

facts.design: 84-ft (per firelookout.com/idahofirelookouts.com; NHLR gives 72-ft) steel Aermotor tower with 7x7-ft cab

access.note: NHLR lists it as available for rental; a nearby cabin is bookable on recreation.gov, but on-tower public access/climbability is not confirmed by any source read.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Ashton Ranger District, Caribou-Targhee National Forest

events.note: Steel Aermotor tower; idahofirelookouts.com gives 1938 for the tower and cabin
Saw extensive service during the Yellowstone fires
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register, nominated by Targhee NF supervisor and forest archaeologist

evidence.quote: The 72-ft steel Aermotor tower, with a 7- by 7-ft cab, was constructed in 1937.
This 84' steel tower, built in 1937, is available for emergencies.

evidence.supports: location near St. Anthony / Fremont County

evidence.quote: Now on standby status, the tower saw extensive service during the Yellowstone Fires of 1988.
1988 – Saw extensive service during Yellowstone fires
We don't yet have a documented staffing history for this lookout.

evidence.supports: added to NHLR 1991, nominated by forest supervisor and archaeologist
evidence.quote: Date Registered November 15, 1991 Nominated by James L. Caswell, Forest Supervisor and Charles G. Willingham, Forest Archaeologist, both of Targhee National Forest

evidence.supports: administered by USFS, Ashton Ranger District, standby, available for rental
evidence.quote: Administered by U.S. Forest Service Cooperators Ashton Ranger District Available for Rental Yes, learn more
The nearby cabin is on the rental program at recreation.gov – https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/234304

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources disagree on both the build year (1937 vs 1938) and the tower's height (72 ft per NHLR vs 84 ft per firelookout.com and idahofirelookouts.com); the record's height_m (25.6 m = 84 ft) matches the latter two.

notes_for_editor: Build year (1937 vs 1938) and tower height (72 ft vs 84 ft) conflict between NHLR and the other two sources; noted in the story rather than resolved. NHLR's own record page says the tower is 'available for rental,' which conflicts a little with the record's access.level of 'unknown' -- worth a look, but I left access as unknown in facts since no source confirms public climbing access, only rental/standby status.
